title: Batch-splitting tests do not verify preservation of input files
reasoning: Both split scenarios assert batch counts, but neither checks which files the batches contain. Returning the first file three times satisfies the line-limit test; repeating the first two files in every batch satisfies the file-limit test. These regressions would omit files from grading while these tests remain green.
recommendation: Expand both existing scenarios to assert that flattening the batches preserves every input file exactly once, alongside the applicable batch limits.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Other scenarios verify file identities when batching does not split small files across multiple batches. They do not protect file preservation at split boundaries.
suggestedRegressionTest: Compare the multiset of flattened output paths with the input paths in both split scenarios, and assert each resulting batch respects its configured limit.
